clue.text: Fairly good judge, following fashion

indicators.note: the judge piece follows the fashion piece, so it is written after it

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or prevailing style
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A critic's lukewarm verdict, given only after the latest trend has been taken into account.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling or passable is fairly good, neither poor nor excellent.

clue.text: Man accepts alternative spirits

indicators.note: accepts means the man piece takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a man is a male
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A fellow agrees to try a different drink or perhaps a different mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits in the sense of a group's mood or confidence: high spirits, good morale.

clue.text: Pour out of brigade canteen

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken from inside the words brigade canteen

explanation.surface: Soldiers serving drinks from the regimental canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour wine gently from bottle into another vessel, leaving sediment behind, is the usual sense.

clue.text: Admiration as Peter's turned about 100

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the numeral
turned means the letters of Peter's are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Peter's, apostrophe ignored
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Peter earns admiration by turning round, perhaps a century in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges PETERS into RESPET, and 'about' puts that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is esteem or high regard, close to admiration in meaning.

clue.text: One responsible for somebody's health after a meal

definitions.text: One responsible for somebody's health after a meal

parts.words: One responsible for somebody's health after a meal
parts.note: sounds like a doctor, but the health is the one drunk to in a toast at a formal dinner, proposed by the master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: Seemingly a medic watching over a diner's wellbeing once the plates are cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: At banquets the master of ceremonies announces speeches and calls on guests to drink healths.

clue.text: April's turned out to be springlike

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of April's are rearranged to form a new word

explanation.surface: The month has turned out to be like spring, as April ought to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'springlike' suggests the season, but it means coiled like a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled spring winds round and round, so springlike shape is a helical curve.

clue.text: Favourite college will get over a bloomer

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
uni is short for university, a college

explanation.surface: A favoured student will get over making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is a mistake on the surface, but here it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and this garden flower is one.

clue.text: Caught on concerning a sled I damaged

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter's subject line

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of a sled I are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to wrecking a toboggan, perhaps after being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch on is to understand or become aware, the same as grasping something.

clue.text: Intelligentsia must be switched on, period — it's uplifting

parts.note: a light switched on is lit
an era is a period of history

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Clever people must be switched on all the time: it's inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns IT into TI, read upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the learned, literary class, and the Latin plural names educated people.

clue.text: Pile of hay's put with wild fruit in carriage

parts.note: a rick is a haystack
the 's of hay's gives S
a haw is the berry of the hawthorn, a wild fruit

explanation.surface: A farm scene: hay stacked up with berries in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as a separate S.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person is a type of carriage.

clue.text: Channel without water mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means a word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a drink taken straight is neat, with no water added

explanation.surface: A dried-up channel, spoken of as though it were a canal without water.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow sea passage between two landmasses, such as Dover's, is a channel.

clue.text: Fast eating that is initially not sparing

indicators.note: eating means the fast piece swallows the other letters

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
ie abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of not is used

explanation.surface: During a fast, eating is at first not allowed, so food is sparing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it is the season of abstinence before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sparing with punishment means being merciful or easy-going towards someone.

clue.text: City in great shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters of in great are jumbled

explanation.surface: A city in a dreadful state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: This Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar is a well-known city.

clue.text: Have a fling then go? It's what some do after retiring!

definitions.text: It's what some do after retiring!

parts.note: to toss is to fling or throw
and can mean then, as in come and see
a turn is a go, as in whose go is it

explanation.surface: A brief affair and then leaving, followed by a joke about what happens at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless sleepers keep shifting and rolling in bed after they turn in for the night.

clue.text: Clear coach's avoiding one father?

indicators.note: avoiding means that letter is left out

parts.note: to coach is to train, so coach's gives trains
I is the Roman numeral one
a father is a parent

explanation.surface: A sports trainer obviously keeps away from one dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops I from TRAINS, leaving TRANS. The question mark flags father as an example of a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear glass lets light through, so you can see straight through it.

clue.text: Features cool spacecraft

parts.note: a film that features an actor stars them
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A trendy sci-fi film features a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction's ships travelling between the stars are vessels for outer space.

clue.text: Grey knight in fix — and others

indicators.note: in means the knight letter is placed inside the fix piece

parts.note: to gum is to stick or fix in place
N is the chess notation for a knight
et al is the Latin abbreviation for and others

explanation.surface: A knight in shining grey armour and his companions in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fix' suggests trouble, but fix is a verb meaning stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull bluish-grey colour named after the bronze alloy once used for cannon.

clue.text: Summons to action from US president, and French come round

parts.note: Donald Trump is a US president
et is French for and
to call is to visit, to come round

explanation.surface: An American president and the French visit, a rallying cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle blast or rallying cry urging people to act is this kind of summons.

clue.text: Attendant coming over poorly gets sack

indicators.note: coming over means the attendant piece covers the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A sick servant comes over and is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like dismissal, but it means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder and loot it.

clue.text: Not a pleasing, deviating type of bowling

indicators.note: deviating means the remaining letters stray from their order
not means the following a is struck out of pleasing

explanation.surface: An unsatisfying cricket delivery that turns off line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes A from PLEASING, leaving PLESING; 'deviating' rearranges that. In cricket, this spin bowling turns from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist-spinner's delivery turning from leg to off is a recognised style of cricket bowling.

clue.text: Junk excessively personal artwork

parts.note: tat is tasteless junk
too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: Ditch overly self-indulgent artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink design on the skin is art worn on one's own body.

clue.text: Covert cult embracing religious class

indicators.note: embracing means the cult piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult
RE is religious education, a school lesson

explanation.surface: A clandestine cult holding its own religious lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert and hidden activities are kept from public knowledge.

clue.text: Leaving South Carolina, motorcyclist or walker

indicators.note: leaving means that state's letters depart from the motorcyclist word

parts.note: a scrambler rides motorcycles over rough country
SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

explanation.surface: Someone quits South Carolina, on a motorbike or on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker strolling the countryside for pleasure is a walker.

clue.text: Humiliate degree-holder briefly seen in river

indicators.note: seen in means the shortened graduate sits inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
grad is short for graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate spotted briefly in a river, embarrassingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to debase or disgrace them, lowering their dignity.

clue.text: Killer struck worker

parts.note: hit is struck
to man a post is to work it; a man is a worker

explanation.surface: A murderer attacked a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired assassin is a professional killer.

clue.text: First couple of questions priest composed to be comic

indicators.note: first couple of means the opening two letters of questions
composed means the letters of priest are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A priest is asked questions, and his composure makes him funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecracking joker who makes witty remarks is a comic.

clue.text: After exercises, Swiss hero rolled over in small ball

indicators.note: after means the hero piece comes behind the exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

indicators.note: rolled over means the hero's name is read backwards

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero

explanation.surface: After a workout, William Tell rolls up into a little ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round pellet is a tiny ball, as of shot or compressed matter.

clue.text: Inconsistent bishop avoids scepticism following fashionable article

indicators.note: following means the doubt piece is written after the others

parts.note: in means fashionable
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: avoids means the bishop letter is left out

parts.note: doubt is scepticism
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A wavering bishop shuns doubt in pursuit of a trendy item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' drops B from DOUBT, giving DOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchy and erratic performance varies in quality, sometimes good and sometimes poor.
